description: JACL Milestone 0 — Value Representation: 64-bit tagged value system with inline types, pointer payloads, inline strings, flag propagation, arithmetic, and comparisons

userStories.title: Define JaclVal type and tag-byte constants
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need the core JaclVal typedef and tag-byte constants so that all modules share a single value representation.
acceptanceCriteria: value/value.h exists following single-header convention (#ifndef VALUE_H / #define VALUE_H for declarations, #ifdef VALUE_IMPLEMENTATION for implementation)
JaclVal is a uint64_t typedef
Tag byte occupies bits 63-56; payload occupies bits 55-0 (56 bits)
Tag byte layout: bit 7 = tainted, bit 6 = secret, bit 5 = error, bits 4-0 = type tag
Mask/shift constants defined: JACL_TAG_SHIFT (56), JACL_TAG_MASK, JACL_PAYLOAD_MASK, JACL_FLAG_TAINTED, JACL_FLAG_SECRET, JACL_FLAG_ERROR, JACL_FLAGS_MASK, JACL_TYPE_MASK
Type tag constants defined for: NIL, BOOL, I32, F32, INLINE_STRING, STRING, VECTOR, MAP, CLOSURE, BIGNUM (exact numeric values are implementation choice)
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Nil and boolean constructors, extractors, and predicates
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need to create and inspect nil and boolean JaclVal values so that control flow and absence-of-value can be represented.
acceptanceCriteria: JACL_NIL constant produces a nil-tagged value with zero payload
JACL_TRUE and JACL_FALSE convenience constants
jacl_bool(bool b) constructor produces a bool-tagged value with 0 or 1 payload
jacl_is_nil(JaclVal v) returns true only for nil-tagged values (ignoring flag bits)
jacl_is_bool(JaclVal v) returns true only for bool-tagged values (ignoring flag bits)
jacl_as_bool(JaclVal v) extracts the boolean payload
Round-trip: jacl_as_bool(jacl_bool(x)) == x for both true and false
value/test_value.c exists with tests using test/test_helpers.h and tracked_allocator
Tests verify nil is not bool, bool is not nil, JACL_TRUE != JACL_FALSE
Test file added to TESTS array in build.sh
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: i32 constructors and extractors
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need to store and retrieve 32-bit signed integers inline in a JaclVal so that integer arithmetic works without heap allocation.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_i32(int32_t n) constructor packs n into the 56-bit payload with i32 type tag
jacl_is_i32(JaclVal v) returns true only for i32-tagged values (ignoring flag bits)
jacl_as_i32(JaclVal v) extracts the int32_t payload
Round-trip: jacl_as_i32(jacl_i32(n)) == n for all int32_t values
Sign extension handled correctly (negative values survive round-trip via masking, not sign extension)
Tests cover: 0, 1, -1, INT32_MAX, INT32_MIN
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: f32 constructors and extractors
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need to store and retrieve 32-bit floats inline in a JaclVal so that floating-point arithmetic works without heap allocation.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_f32(float f) constructor packs f into the 56-bit payload via bit-cast (memcpy, not conversion) with f32 type tag
jacl_is_f32(JaclVal v) returns true only for f32-tagged values (ignoring flag bits)
jacl_as_f32(JaclVal v) extracts the float payload via bit-cast (memcpy)
Round-trip: jacl_as_f32(jacl_f32(f)) is bitwise identical to f for all tested values
Tests cover: 0.0f, -0.0f, 1.0f, -1.0f, FLT_MAX, FLT_MIN, FLT_EPSILON, INFINITY, -INFINITY, NAN
NaN round-trips correctly (bitwise comparison via memcmp, not just isnan())
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Pointer-payload constructors and extractors
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need to pack heap pointers into JaclVal for types that don't fit inline (strings, vectors, maps, closures, bignums) so that heap objects participate in the tagged value system.
acceptanceCriteria: Constructors for each pointer-carrying type tag: jacl_string_ptr(void *p), jacl_vector_ptr(void *p), jacl_map_ptr(void *p), jacl_closure_ptr(void *p), jacl_bignum_ptr(void *p)
Each constructor stores the pointer in the low 56 bits with the appropriate type tag in the high byte
jacl_as_ptr(JaclVal v) extracts the raw pointer with tag byte masked off
Type predicates: jacl_is_string(v), jacl_is_vector(v), jacl_is_map(v), jacl_is_closure(v), jacl_is_bignum(v) — each ignores flag bits
Round-trip: pointer survives pack/unpack unchanged
Compile-time assert that pointers fit in 56 bits (user-space addresses on x86-64/ARM64 use at most 48-52 bits)
Tests use malloc'd aligned objects to verify pointer integrity across pack/unpack
This milestone does NOT define heap object layouts — only the JaclVal packing side
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Inline string packing and unpacking
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need to store short strings (0-7 bytes) directly in the 56-bit payload so that common short strings (command names, flags, short identifiers) require zero heap allocation.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_inline_string(const char *s, size_t len) packs up to 7 bytes into the payload with INLINE_STRING type tag
Length is determined by null-termination within the 7-byte payload: first null byte or 7 bytes, whichever comes first
Inline strings must NOT contain null bytes (null is the terminator, not data)
jacl_is_inline_string(JaclVal v) distinguishes inline strings from heap string pointers (different type tags)
jacl_inline_string_len(JaclVal v) returns the length (0-7)
jacl_inline_string_get(JaclVal v, char *buf, size_t buflen) copies the string bytes into a caller-provided buffer and null-terminates
Round-trip: pack then unpack yields identical bytes and length for all valid lengths
Tests cover: empty string (len 0), single char, 6 bytes, 7 bytes (max), strings with various non-null byte values
Test that INLINE_STRING type tag is distinct from STRING (heap pointer) type tag
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Tainted/secret/error flag manipulation
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need to get, set, and clear the metadata flags (tainted, secret, error) on any JaclVal so that security and error metadata can flow through the system.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_is_tainted(v) / jacl_set_tainted(v) / jacl_clear_tainted(v) — get/set/clear bit 7 of tag byte
jacl_is_secret(v) / jacl_set_secret(v) / jacl_clear_secret(v) — get/set/clear bit 6 of tag byte
jacl_is_error(v) / jacl_set_error(v) / jacl_clear_error(v) — get/set/clear bit 5 of tag byte
set/clear functions return a new JaclVal (value semantics, not mutation)
Setting a flag preserves the type tag and payload exactly
Clearing a flag preserves the type tag and payload exactly
Multiple flags can be set simultaneously (e.g., tainted + error)
Tests verify flag independence (setting one doesn't affect others)
Tests verify flags work correctly with all value types: nil, bool, i32, f32, pointer, inline string
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Flag propagation helpers
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need helpers that combine flags from operands so that binary operations automatically propagate tainted/secret/error metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_propagate_flags(JaclVal a, JaclVal b) returns the OR of both values' flag bits (tainted, secret, error) as a uint64_t mask
jacl_apply_flags(JaclVal result, uint64_t flags) applies flag bits onto a result value, preserving its type tag and payload
If either operand is error-flagged, the propagated flags include the error flag
If either operand is tainted, the propagated flags include the tainted flag
If either operand is secret, the propagated flags include the secret flag
Tests verify all 8 flag combinations per operand (2^3), spot-checking key combinations: no flags, one flag each, mixed flags, all flags on both
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Complete type predicate set and type_tag extractor
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need a complete set of type-checking predicates and a raw type_tag extractor so that any code handling JaclVal can quickly determine its type.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_type_tag(JaclVal v) extracts the 5-bit type tag (masking out flag bits)
Predicates defined for every type: jacl_is_nil, jacl_is_bool, jacl_is_i32, jacl_is_f32, jacl_is_inline_string, jacl_is_string, jacl_is_vector, jacl_is_map, jacl_is_closure, jacl_is_bignum
All predicates ignore flag bits — an error-flagged i32 still returns true for jacl_is_i32
Each predicate returns false for all other types (no false positives)
Tests create one value of each type and verify every predicate against every type (NxN matrix)
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: i32 arithmetic operations with flag propagation
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need arithmetic operations on i32 JaclVal operands so that the VM can execute integer math with automatic flag propagation.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_add_i32(a, b) returns i32 JaclVal sum with flags propagated from both operands
jacl_sub_i32(a, b) returns i32 JaclVal difference with propagated flags
jacl_mul_i32(a, b) returns i32 JaclVal product with propagated flags
jacl_div_i32(a, b) returns i32 JaclVal quotient with propagated flags; division by zero returns an error-flagged value
jacl_mod_i32(a, b) returns i32 JaclVal remainder with propagated flags; mod by zero returns an error-flagged value
jacl_neg_i32(a) returns negated i32 JaclVal with preserved flags
If either operand has the error flag set, the error operand is returned immediately (no computation performed)

Tests cover: basic arithmetic (3+4=7, 10-3=7, 6*7=42, 10/3=3, 10%3=1), negative numbers, division by zero, mod by zero, error propagation, flag propagation through arithmetic, INT32_MIN edge cases (e.g., -INT32_MIN overflow)
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: f32 arithmetic operations with flag propagation
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need arithmetic operations on f32 JaclVal operands so that the VM can execute floating-point math with automatic flag propagation.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_add_f32(a, b) returns f32 JaclVal sum with propagated flags
jacl_sub_f32(a, b) returns f32 JaclVal difference with propagated flags
jacl_mul_f32(a, b) returns f32 JaclVal product with propagated flags
jacl_div_f32(a, b) returns f32 JaclVal quotient with propagated flags; follows IEEE 754 for division by zero (returns inf, NOT an error-flagged value)
jacl_neg_f32(a) returns negated f32 JaclVal with preserved flags
If either operand has the error flag set, the error operand is returned immediately (no computation performed)
Tests cover: basic arithmetic, negative numbers, inf/nan behavior (inf + 1 = inf, 0/0 = nan, 1/0 = inf), error propagation, flag propagation through arithmetic
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Comparison operations with flag propagation
userStories.description: As a runtime developer, I need comparison operations that return JaclVal booleans so that the VM can evaluate conditionals with proper flag propagation.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_eq(a, b) returns JaclVal bool; values are equal if same type tag AND same payload bits (ignoring flags)
jacl_lt_i32(a, b) / jacl_gt_i32(a, b) / jacl_le_i32(a, b) / jacl_ge_i32(a, b) — signed i32 comparisons returning JaclVal bool
jacl_lt_f32(a, b) / jacl_gt_f32(a, b) / jacl_le_f32(a, b) / jacl_ge_f32(a, b) — f32 comparisons returning JaclVal bool
All comparison results carry propagated flags from both operands
If either operand has the error flag set, comparisons return the error operand (not a bool)
jacl_eq handles: nil == nil is true, true == true is true, false == false is true, true != false, nil != false, cross-type comparisons return false
jacl_eq for inline strings compares payload bytes (bytewise equality)
jacl_eq for pointer types compares pointer values (pointer equality, not structural)
Tests cover: same-type equality, cross-type inequality, nil comparisons, i32 ordering, f32 ordering, flag propagation on results, error short-circuit
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99
